examples.en: Thanks to timely help, we got through the crisis.
That announcement came at just the right time.
Thank you for getting in touch at just the right time.

examples.ko: 지금 대출을 받는 건 시기적절하지 않아요.
examples.en: Taking out a loan now isn't well-timed.

examples.ko: 이 책은 지금 읽기에 시기적절해 보여요.
examples.en: This book seems well-timed to read right now.
Opinions are split on whether the government's measures were timely.

explain: '적절하다'는 때와 상관없이 알맞다는 뜻이고, 시기적절하다는 때가 딱 맞다는 점을 강조해요. '시기적절한 조치/도움/발표'처럼 많이 써요. 반대로 너무 이르다고 할 때는 '시기상조'라고 해요.
explain_en: '적절하다' means suitable in general, while 시기적절하다 stresses that the timing is just right. It is common in phrases like '시기적절한 조치/도움/발표'. When something is too early, the opposite idea is expressed with '시기상조'.

examples.ko: 윗물이 맑아야 아랫물이 맑다는 속담이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a proverb that the lower stream is clear only if the upper stream is clear.

examples.ko: 윗물에서 쓰레기를 버리면 아래 마을이 피해를 봐요.
examples.en: If people dump trash upstream, the villages below suffer.
The factory polluted the upstream water.

examples.ko: 윗물 쪽 마을에서는 물을 아껴 쓰자고 했어요.
examples.en: The villages on the upstream side said we should save water.
The upstream water is clear, but the downstream water is cloudy.
Change has to start from the top of the company.

explain: 강이나 개울의 위쪽 물이라는 뜻이지만, 윗사람이나 조직의 위쪽을 비유할 때도 자주 써요. 반대말은 '아랫물'이고, 속담 때문에 '윗물이 맑아야…'라는 말로 많이 알려져 있어요.

phrases.example: 윗물이 맑아야 아랫물이 맑다고, 사장님이 먼저 모범을 보여야 해요.
phrases.en: Those at the top must set a good example for those below.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람이 바르게 행동해야 아랫사람도 따라서 바르게 행동한다는 속담이에요. 리더의 책임을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning that people below will behave well only if those above do. It is used when talking about a leader's responsibility.

explain_en: It means the water in the upper part of a river or stream, but it is also often used figuratively for people at the top of an organization. The opposite is '아랫물', and it is best known through the proverb '윗물이 맑아야…'.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 공기가 청정해서 살기 좋아요.
examples.en: The air in this village is pure, so it's a nice place to live.

examples.ko: 청정한 바다에서 잡은 생선이라 아주 신선해요.
examples.en: The fish was caught in clean seas, so it's very fresh.
This is an unpolluted area, so its farm products are famous.

examples.ko: 공기가 청정하다고 해서 와 봤는데 정말 맑아요.
examples.en: I heard the air was pure so I came, and it really is clear.

examples.ko: 공기가 청정하지 않은 날에는 마스크를 써요.
examples.en: On days when the air isn't clean, I wear a mask.

examples.ko: 계곡물이 청정하게 보여도 그냥 마시면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Even if the valley water looks pure, you shouldn't drink it as it is.

explain: '깨끗하다'보다 격식 있고, 공기, 물, 바다, 자연처럼 오염이 없는 환경에 써요. 방이나 옷이 깨끗할 때는 쓰지 않아요. '청정 지역', '청정 해역'처럼 광고나 안내문에서 많이 보고, '공기청정기'에도 들어 있는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is more formal than '깨끗하다' and is used for unpolluted environments such as air, water, seas and nature. You would not use it for a clean room or clean clothes. You often see it in ads and notices as in '청정 지역' and '청정 해역', and it is part of '공기청정기' (air purifier).
